decisions.reason: The September 21 vendor case study is within the September 17–October 16 freshness window and describes a workshop-to-survey brand-tracking workflow for a US beverage brand. However, it documents no specific AI research capability, small-business access or costs. Quantilope has a commercial interest in the customer success story; missing sample, recruitment, questionnaire, baseline timings and outcome measures leave its speed and commercial-growth claims unsupported. The quoted Quirk’s presentation is reused testimony, not independent corroboration or evidence of a new event.

The October 9 article is timely but sells tickets to TechCrunch’s own San Francisco event rather than documenting an AI workflow for customer, competitor or market research. Its direct commercial incentive and unmeasured 'highest-ROI' pitch provide no inspectable evidence of research quality, practical effort or small-business savings.

The supplied October 2 publication metadata places this substantive methodological guidance within the freshness window. Its practical contribution is an inspectable constraint on AI-assisted interview and feedback synthesis: 'Every sticky note ... should trace back to a specific research artifact,' with unsupported notes labeled assumptions. The AI section explicitly distinguishes organizing existing evidence from generating evidence. Accept for source-linked review practices, not demonstrated accuracy, bias removal or time savings: no comparative evaluation is supplied. Small-business deployments, non-English transfer and customer-data handling are unexamined; no specific sponsorship is disclosed. The evidence does not establish whether this revises an older article, so describe the supplied guidance without claiming empathy mapping itself is new.

The October 1 vendor announcement documents a concrete competitor-monitoring capability: API responses reportedly include dates, competitor tags, full text and source links, with examples of AI briefings and product-update workflows. This supports an attributed capability report and a source-traceability pilot, not independent effectiveness findings. Crayon benefits commercially; unnamed beta examples and 'getting started takes minutes' lack a named baseline, setup/checking measurements or costs. Pricing, small-business access, technical burden, geographic coverage and handling of call and win/loss data remain unknown. Repeated clean-data and easy-integration claims within the announcement are not separate corroboration.
